shots.text: They drilled a fourteen inch hole, and a whole lake vanished.
You see, Lake Peigneur in Louisiana was only about ten feet deep.
Under it sat a salt mine. On top floated an oil rig, drilling for Texaco.
On November twentieth, nineteen eighty, the drill bit got stuck.
A stuck bit is a small problem. Then the rig began to tilt.
A whirlpool opened, and the lake poured into the mine.
In three hours, three and a half billion gallons of water were gone.
The rig tipped over and sank. Barges spun around and went under.
You see, fresh water dissolves salt, like sugar in hot tea. The hole grew wider and wider.
A worker sounded the alarm. Fifty miners ran for the exits, and every one made it out alive.
So the canal ran backward, making Louisiana's tallest waterfall ever.
Gulf water refilled the lake. Today it's salty, and the salt dome beneath it stores natural gas.
